overview: This bill extends funding authority for Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) programs created by the Save Our Seas 2.0 Act, a 2020 law aimed at reducing plastic and other trash that ends up in oceans and waterways. These programs give grants to help communities improve recycling and waste-management systems and keep trash out of water. Under current law, Congress authorized money for these programs only through 2025; this bill extends that authorization through 2030. It also makes a small wording fix to the law. The Senate passed it, and as of November 20, 2025, it was being held at the House desk awaiting action.
for: Supporters say the bill keeps established programs against marine trash running for five more years, giving communities steady support to improve recycling and keep plastic out of oceans.
against: Critics say extending the programs authorizes more federal grant spending without first showing how well the existing grants have reduced ocean trash.
